summary: Full E2E validation of the new Crew module (backend + frontend). Backend pytest suite: 28/29 passed (1 minor failure from destructive cleanup — see note). Frontend E2E: owner login by username, legacy owner (blank username), sales legacy (blank username), crew role restricted nav, Junior forced-change flow, Javante My Jobs + status workflow (En Route → Arrived → In Progress → Complete with notes), photo upload, GPS-consent dialog + clock in/out (no-GPS warning path), days-off marking, owner Crew page all 5 tabs (Team/Schedule/Time/Live map/Report), assignment create+edit+conflict warnings + force-save, notifications bell with unread badge + mark-all-read, CSV export — all working. Junior password was changed from HaulCrew2026! → JunCrew2026! and test_credentials.md was updated.

minor.issue: Response is wrapped ({"users":[...]}, {"trucks":[...]}, {"entries":[...]}) — inconsistent with rest of API (e.g., /api/assignments also wrapped but /api/reports/labor is a bare dict). Not a bug; just note for API-shape docs.

integration_issues.issue: While logged in as crew (Javante), the frontend probes some owner-only endpoints and logs 8x 'Failed to load resource: 403' in the browser console. Silent to the user, but adds noise. Suggest guarding those fetches with role checks.

issues: When Javante taps a future day cell to mark UNAVAILABLE, the DOM class updates (confirmed) and backend persists (verified via GET /api/crew/availability) but the visual cue (red background) was not obvious in the screenshot for the outlined cell (data-date=2026-07-26). The border/color could be higher-contrast so crew clearly see the day is marked OFF.

Punches with <1 minute duration render as '0h' with no seconds/minutes formatting. Not a bug (integer rounding), but under 60s a 'seconds' fallback would be friendlier for testing/first-clock-in feedback.

action_items: OPTIONAL: gate crew-view API probes so they don't fire owner-only endpoints (403 console noise).
OPTIONAL: strengthen the visual OFF/red styling on daysoff-day-cell so crew clearly see the toggle worked.
NOTE: test_credentials.md was updated to reflect Junior's new password (JunCrew2026!).

NOTE: test_create_reset_deactivate_user in backend suite is destructive by email; re-running back-to-back will fail because the deactivated user's email lingers. Consider randomizing email suffix (uuid) or deleting instead of deactivating in a future refactor.
critical_code_review_comments: backend/server.py is 1717 lines — well over the recommended 700-line split point. Recommend splitting into modules: auth.py, crew.py, timeclock.py, assignments.py, notifications.py, storage.py.

Assignment PATCH requires the full AssignmentPayload — even a minor arrival_time edit needs the whole crew/truck/address block re-sent. That's the correct semantics for POST but slightly heavier than a partial PATCH; frontend's edit modal must round-trip the whole document. Verified working but note for future.
assignment_warnings() double-appends duplicate warnings when the same crew member is on two other assignments — could produce noisy warning lists on busy days.
/api/notifications shape: returns {'notifications':[...], 'unread':N} whereas /api/notifications/read-all returns just {'ok':True}. Consistent enough.

Recommended future fix: randomize the email each run (uuid) so the test is fully isolated.
